UPSTREAM: mb/google/hatch: Re-configure GPP_A12 as GPO before entering sleep GPP_A12 has a Native3 (SX_EXIT_HOLDOFF#) mode, which allows to delay resuming to S0. If this pad is not locked and platform was not initially designed for this functionality, malware could reconfigure this pads setting under OS (switch to Native3), which would make platform not able to resume until G3 is applied. To prevent misuse of this pad, re-configure this pad before entering S3 and S5 to guarantee that the pad configuration is correct. BUG=b:128686027 Change-Id: If0a8e5fb0df00931cdcd083cd03a2f15832556cb Signed-off-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@google.com> Original-Commit-Id: c41b0e8ea3b2714bf6d6d88a6b66c333c6919f07 Original-Change-Id: I1e7979baa491acf2c56d223afb4618f0f6429e37 Original-Signed-off-by: Krishna Prasad Bhat <krishna.p.bhat.d@intel.com> Original-Reviewed-on: https://review.coreboot.org/c/coreboot/+/32111 Original-Tested-by: build bot (Jenkins) <no-reply@coreboot.org> Original-Reviewed-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1547566 Commit-Ready: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org> Tested-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org>

tast-tests: Handle bad data in security.SandboxedServices. Make further changes to security.SandboxedServices to try to handle bad or missing process data. We sometimes see missing /ns/mnt links even while processes are still in the 'R' state. Remove the previous hacks that ignored errors while in the 'Z' or 'D' states, and instead just ignore ENOENT for /ns/mnt, /ns/pid, and /mounts, and additionally EINVAL for /mounts (since I locally observed that this can be returned for zombie processes). Also refactor the code that checks required sandboxing features for each process. BUG=chromium:936703 TEST=manual: ran against a DUT with a zombie process Change-Id: Iadc5e9201e1c9260dba7d45024d24ce1a3755c31 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1548655 Commit-Ready: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org> Tested-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Shuhei Takahashi <nya@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hidehiko Abe <hidehiko@chromium.org>

npcx7_evb: illustrate the flash configuration of npcx7m7wc There are only 512 Kbytes of internal flash in Rev.C of npcx7m7w (i.e. npcx7m7wc.) It is different from the Rev.B of npcx7m7w (i.e. npcx7m7wb.) This CL illustrates how to set the flash type and flash size when chip variant is npcx7m7wc. BRANCH=none BUG=none TEST=pass "make buildall". TEST=with related CLs, switch to different chip variant in build.mk; build and flash the image; make sure each EC image can boot up on EVB or internal testing board of different chip variant. Change-Id: I2b50c7a023b1634ed4a200cb826532174baae117 Signed-off-by: CHLin <CHLIN56@nuvoton.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1543063 Commit-Ready: CH Lin <chlin56@nuvoton.com> Tested-by: CH Lin <chlin56@nuvoton.com> Reviewed-by: Aseda Aboagye <aaboagye@chromium.org>
